status.en: 226 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 226 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen killed seven civilians in a Plateau community and shot Islamic cleric Yahaya Masussuka dead in Katsina state, while bandits attacked APC supporters ahead of a rally in Katsina. In Taraba state, gunmen killed at least 62 people in Binnari, prompting thousands to flee, and in Kaduna, kidnappers abducted six residents from the Millennium City estate. The Nigerian Correctional Service reported that armed escorts fired warning shots during an attack in Rivers that left one dead. A convoy crash in Niger state killed four students and a driver. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn drepte syv sivile i et samfunn på Plateau og skjøt den islamske lærde Yahaya Masussuka i hjel i Katsina-delstaten, mens banditter angrep APC-tilhengere før et møte i Katsina. I Taraba-delstaten drepte væpnede menn minst 62 personer i Binnari, noe som fikk tusenvis til å flykte, og i Kaduna bortførte kidnappere seks innbyggere fra Millennium City-området. Det nigerianske fengselvesenet rapporterte at bevæpnede eskorter skjøt advarselsskudd under et angrep i Rivers som førte til ett dødsfall. En konvoøyulykke i Niger-delstaten drepte fire studenter og en sjåfør. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
